comparator.name: South and Southeast Asian Studies
comparator.route: Hindi language; Modern South and Modern Southeast Asia specialisation; Leiden third-year programme
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026-27 Leiden Study Guide and public product API define 60 EC in each year. The coherent pathway selects Hindi as the first language in the current curriculum listing, Introduction to the Study of Islam and Classics of Asia as the first-listed year-one restricted choices, and the first-listed Modern South and Modern Southeast Asia year-two specialisation. Within that 20-EC specialisation, the first four listed 5-EC modules are selected; Buddhist Art supplies the separate 5-EC SSEAS elective without duplicating a selected module. Year three selects the Leiden programme rather than study abroad: Hindi Literature (10 EC) plus Tantric Buddhism (5 EC), followed by the 10-EC BA thesis. The two published 15-EC components of genuine elective space remain open. These selections are made independently of UCR fit and account for exactly 180 EC.

routeSelection.route: Hindi language; Modern South and Modern Southeast Asia specialisation; Leiden third-year programme
routeSelection.basis: The generic target requires a language sequence, a year-two non-language specialisation and a year-three Leiden or study-abroad pathway to instantiate 180 EC. The official programme presents all four regional languages as valid and the two non-language specialisations as alternatives. Hindi and Modern South and Modern Southeast Asia appear first in the current curriculum structure, and the Leiden third-year programme is the first-listed pathway; these choices were made as neutral tie-breaks without reference to UCR fit.

programmes.label: South and Southeast Asian Studies at Leiden University

exception.reason: Leiden's 180-EC South and Southeast Asian Studies pathway integrates 50 EC of progressive Hindi language and literature with regional history, cultures, religion, politics, economics, humanities methods, specialist seminars and a region-focused bachelor thesis. UCR offers no Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian language course and no South or Southeast Asian studies sequence. Its broadly comparative history, politics, philosophy, religion and literature courses could support occasional perspectives on the region, but they cannot make 23 non-PPD courses contribute concretely to a South and Southeast Asia-centred academic concept or reproduce the language-based cultural and source work that defines the Leiden degree.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-27 curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: year one combines 30 EC of compulsory regional study with 20 EC of one language and two 5-EC restricted choices; year two combines 15 EC compulsory, 20 EC continued language, a 20-EC non-language specialisation and a 5-EC SSEAS elective; year three combines a 5-EC seminar, 15 EC of the selected Leiden pathway, a 10-EC BA thesis and 30 EC of genuine elective space. The selected Hindi and Modern South and Modern Southeast Asia pathway is coherent across all three years and preserves every component exactly once.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. The workbook contains no Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian course and no course dedicated to South or Southeast Asia. MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature includes isolated Indian literary examples, GOSPHIL214 Philosophy of Mind briefly considers Buddhist thought, and general history, politics, sociology, economics, religion, art and literature courses supply transferable disciplinary methods. Those isolated references and general methods do not constitute a regional language sequence, sustained area-study progression or region-specific source training. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore be built chiefly from adjacent global or comparative courses and would misrepresent the defining regional and linguistic core.
